title: Stripe didn't buy OpenRouter but invokes 'singularity' to avoid going public
summary: Stripe clarifies it didn't acquire OpenRouter and uses the idea of technological singularity as justification to postpone its IPO.

title: Gameplay and map of GTA VI leaked while Rockstar tries to contain biggest leak in years
summary: A hacker publishes gameplay and full GTA 6 map in protest over digital-only launch, and Rockstar partially contains the leak.

title: Seasonic launches first ATX PSU with 80 PLUS Ruby certification, highest energy efficiency
summary: The Seasonic PRIME RX-1600 achieves 80 PLUS Ruby certification at 115V, setting a new efficiency standard for power supplies.

title: Nvidia starts shipping H200 chips to China after Beijing eases import restrictions
summary: ByteDance and Tencent receive first H200 shipments, though most licensed chips must remain in Hong Kong due to energy limitations.

title: China orders removal of its custom Windows 10 version for government use ahead of schedule
summary: Beijing turns its back on Microsoft and eliminates Windows 10 adapted for its administration, accelerating transition to domestic systems.

title: DDR4 memory to rise 50% in price next quarter due to supply crisis
summary: Manufacturers warn of drastic DDR4 price increase due to chip shortage and high demand for AI servers.

title: Intel Core Ultra 9 4950K appears as world's fastest consumer CPU and points to new Nova Lake architecture
summary: First tests and sightings of Core Ultra 9 4950K suggest record performance and possible naming change to Nova Lake-S.

title: The Blood of Dawnwalker lowers requirements: RTX 5090 not needed to play at 4K 60 FPS
summary: Rebel Wolves' RPG updates technical specs and confirms mandatory DLSS, FSR, and XeSS support at launch.

title: Anthropic allows any lab to use language agents to design complete proteins
summary: Claude demonstrated designing functional proteins against 14 of 15 targets in lab tests, and now Anthropic opens entire protein design stack.

title: Developers create macOS drivers for obsolete hardware using AI and Linux containers
summary: One user programs a driver for their Drobo and another uses Claude to adapt a Windows-only printer, demonstrating viability of 'vibe-coding' drivers on macOS.
